based_on: Staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 70 Gerrard Street East under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
If there are no objections to the designation, staff recommend that City Council authorize the City Solicitor to introduce a bill to designate the property.
The property at 70 Gerrard Street East is on the north side of Gerrard Street East, at the northeast corner of Church Street, in the Downtown Yonge East neighbourhood.
The building was constructed around 1845 in the Georgian style and was substantially altered in 1886 in the Queen Anne Revival style.
Staff and a heritage consultant determined that the property has cultural heritage value and meets six of the nine provincial criteria for municipal heritage designation.
A property may be designated if it meets two or more of the nine provincial criteria.
Heritage designation allows City Council to review proposed alterations or demolitions to the property and enforce heritage property standards and maintenance.
There are no financial impacts to the City resulting from the recommendations in this report.
